**Retirements:** Starting with the Chairman (former Chairman if vacant), clockwise, each player may retire each pensioner to a prize. Pay its printed cost, move the member to the prize and gain printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends to establish display-selection order, then pay bank. Prizes may incur upkeep and window taxes. Unused pensioners do not remain for another turn.

**Prestige:** Players who retired at least one pensioner must each take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties: most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. Acting player may peek at display blackmails. **Do not replace a chosen/discarded card during selection. If the display becomes empty, immediately skip every remaining eligible player.** Finish the display step by **discarding all remaining cards and refilling exactly three: prestige faceup, blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card**. Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies.

source_quotes.quote:
Starting with the Chairman title holder, clockwise, each player resolves their family action:

1. Check where your opportunity marker was **at phase start** (it begins off the board).
2. Choose a main family action: take it once, or **may take it twice if the marker already matched it**.
3. **Place/move the opportunity marker onto your chosen main action.**
4. After the main action, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant its extra action. This extra action is never doubled by the marker and never moves the marker.

If placing a family piece with none in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize's printed VP. This applies to firm-share creation too. If no family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.

| Family action | Effect |
|---|---|
| Enlist Writer | Place a member in any Presidency's Writers box. With at least four vacant offices, place one additional writer **once this turn**, so a doubled Writer action can place three total. |
| Enlist Officer | Place a member in Officers-in-Training. |
| Purchase Luxury | Pay bank £4; gain luxury, 2 VP while owned, and its window icon; social enterprise. |
| Purchase Shipyard | Pay bank £2; take shipyard and place its matching ship **unfitted on that shipyard**, not in a sea zone. Shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. |
| Purchase Workshop | Pay bank £5; take workshop; manufacturing enterprise, two votes, £1 bonus; worth 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. |
| Seek Share | Place a member on an empty Stock Exchange space and pay bank: the five queue spaces are £2, £3, £3, £4, £5 (two distinct £3 spaces). It is an applicant, not yet a share. |

grades.reader_quote: 1. A President declares regions for Trade, including the home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President’s treasury buys one die; subtract one per declared nonhome region. Failure can be retried during operations if affordable, but each President can have at most one successful Trade per turn, and failed attempts/retries remain that President’s uninterrupted opportunity. A successful Trade has capacity of one order per ship in that Presidency’s sea zone and does not exhaust ships. Fill as many as possible in declared regions: first writer goes to home port; every later order extends the connected route filled during this same Trade. Writers from another Presidency cannot extend the route; writers do not limit capacity, so use all writers then continue using filled-order tokens for remaining ships. No President may fill another President’s home region, even if vacant. Balance rises by each order’s printed value, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn. The President gets £1 from the bank per order and writer owners get £1 per placed writer.

Success fill as many orders as possible in declared regions, one per ship, first home port then adjacent own placed writers. Use filled tokens if writers exhausted. Cannot fill another Presidency home region even vacant. Company receives printed order values, President £1 per filled order, writer owner £1 per writer placed; at most one successful trade per President per turn. Revenue exception: under Deregulation an order already filled by a firm this turn pays the Company half listed value, rounded down; President and writer bonuses remain unchanged.

source_quotes.quote:
Each President chooses order of its Commander, Governors and its own Trade. Must allow each position an opportunity but Commander/Governors may decline. Each position finishes all actions before next begins. Trade can go before/after Commander or any Governor but cannot interrupt another position. If President vacant, Chairman sets order only: cannot trade or approve local alliance purchases.

Declare regions for Trade: include home region, and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 President's treasury buys one die; subtract one per declared nonhome region. Failure can be retried during operations if affordable; catastrophe removes President. At most **one successful Trade per President per turn**. Failed attempts and retries belong to that President's uninterrupted opportunity; another position cannot act between its attempts.

**Successful Trade capacity is one order per ship in this Presidency's sea zone. Trade does not exhaust ships.** Fill as many orders as possible within declared regions. First writer goes to home port. Every later order must extend the connected route filled during this same Presidency's Trade. **Writers from another Presidency cannot extend this route**, even when adjacent. **Writers do not limit capacity: use all available writers, then continue filling with filled-order tokens for the remaining ships.** Those tokens continue this Trade's own route. No President may fill another President's home region, even if its office vacant. Increase Balance by each order's printed value, **or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn under Deregulation**. President earns bank £1 per order; writer owners earn £1 per writer placed. Separate adjacent writers from different Presidencies with dividers for correct return at Refresh.

grades.reader_quote: 1. A Commander may target their own Presidency’s home, any associated region, or any region bordering an associated region. source_quotes.quote:
**Attacks on Company:** An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve attacks in this order: **primary Crisis first**, then secondary regions in **Bombay → Madras → Bengal** Army order. **Within each Presidency, that Commander chooses the order of its associated regions.** Attack strengths are distinct:

- **Primary normal Crisis:** normal Invasion/Rebellion attack strength **plus unrest in its target region**.
- **Primary Foreign Invasion:** the ordinary attack die, with no added unrest (designer ruling in FAQ).
- **Every secondary Rebellion:** **only the number of unrest cubes in that secondary region**; no event modifier or empire strength.

**Mounting defense — first identify who acts:**

| Defense office situation | Acting player |
|---|---|
| Associated Commander occupied | That Commander chooses and exhausts pieces; normal trophy gains/losses apply. |
| Commander vacant | **Military Affairs itself acts in the Commander's stead**, choosing pieces; gains/loses **no trophies**. |
| Commander AND Military Affairs vacant | **Chairman chooses pieces** and gains/loses **no trophies**. |

This is acting for the defense, **not appointing a new Commander**. The acting player must exhaust active Army pieces equal to Crisis strength, or as many as possible. Local alliances provide printed strength usable once; **their strength cannot be split among more than one purpose**. The printed comparison has these results:

| Printed strength comparison | Attack and defense result |
|---|---|
| Newly exhausted pieces **EQUAL** Crisis strength | **The attack FAILS; defense SUCCEEDS.** Remove all unrest in the attacked region; Commander gains one trophy. If this defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one attacker tower if possible. |
| Newly exhausted pieces **DO NOT EQUAL** Crisis strength | **The attack SUCCEEDS; defense FAILS.** Perform Region Loss. If the successful primary Crisis was an Invasion, apply empire creation/growth. |

**Unresolved counting boundary:** This table reproduces the printed test; it does not determine how an indivisible alliance's excess strength is counted. The strength-2-alliance versus strength-1-attack outcome remains unresolved; see the source gap below.

**Unresolved core source gap — excess alliance strength in defense:** Rules p22 says local-alliance strength can defend and cannot be split among more than one purpose. Page 33 requires newly exhausted Army pieces to equal Crisis strength. The available primary material does not explicitly settle whether a strength-2 alliance can successfully defend a strength-1 attack, or how unused excess strength is counted. No definitive ruling is asserted here. A publisher/designer clarification of that concrete case is needed; this summary remains unverified and its QA is incomplete.

**Foreign Invasion and unrest:** Cole Wehrle clarified on April 30, 2023 that unrest does **not** add to a Foreign Invasion's primary attack strength or determine its resulting tower levels. Use the ordinary die roll for both attack strength and halving to create towers; the event still uses the Company-defense procedure and its secondary unrest attacks. Do not apply the normal primary Crisis's added unrest to this special event. [Designer ruling](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2962161/article/42192767#42192767). **On a successful Foreign Invasion, close all orders in the target region once; if they are already all closed, Cascade instead.** Region Loss does not close them a second time: its additional closure is only for a normal Invasion Crisis.

| Choice | Eligibility and commitment |
|---|---|
| Trade zone/home port | Commit a secret cash bid from London treasury. The selected home port must be **open when filled**; strategy selection itself does not open it. |
| Hobnob | No bid, trade or dividends. Still pay expenses; retain previous dividend marker for retirement. |

**Reveal cash bids simultaneously, but keep strategy cards facedown until their matching Presidency begins.**

At beginning of associated Presidency's operations, before any actions, matching firms reveal strategy and roll one die per committed £1, paying bid to bank. At least one 1/2 permits trade. **Fill only OPEN orders**, as many as possible up to **ships + 1**, starting strategy home port, always tracing through its own filled route back there. **Each firm may fill any particular order only ONCE per turn; it cannot refill its OWN earlier order.** Place filled tokens; revenue goes to India treasury. A firm may refill an order filled by a DIFFERENT firm or the Company this turn; Company may refill firms' orders. A previously filled order pays **half listed revenue, rounded down**, not repeated full value. Advance firm Value one space per full £6 added to India treasury this turn.

**Successful Trade capacity is one order per ship in this Presidency's sea zone. Trade does not exhaust ships.** Fill as many orders as possible within declared regions. First writer goes to home port. Every later order must extend the connected route filled during this same Presidency's Trade. **Writers from another Presidency cannot extend this route**, even when adjacent. **Writers do not limit capacity: use all available writers, then continue filling with filled-order tokens for the remaining ships.** Those tokens continue this Trade's own route. No President may fill another President's home region, even if its office vacant. Increase Balance by each order's printed value, **or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn under Deregulation**. President earns bank £1 per order; writer owners earn £1 per writer placed. Separate adjacent writers from different Presidencies with dividers for correct return at Refresh.

grades.expected_answer: Enterprises incl prestige and Company shares by Power track (bottom two zero); passed laws and trophies +1 each, PM+2, applicable card power incl blackmail faceup/down and spouse. Most/second points based final turn board table; tied first each lower award only, no other award; tied second nothing. Final VP tie most windows then PM clockwise.
grades.observed_answer: 1. Power counts enterprises and Company shares at their current Power-track rates (bottom two positions are zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for the PM, and printed card power, including faceup or facedown blackmail and applicable spouse. Most/second awards are 3/1 VP on final turns 1–3, 5/2 on turns 4–6, and 8/4 on turns 7–8. A tie for first awards only the lower award to each tied player; there is no other award. Tied second place gets no award. Highest final VP wins; ties go to most windows, then clockwise from PM.
grades.summary_evidence: Scoring > Power award and victory tie rules.

**Final retirements/failure card:**

| Company outcome | Final retirement or failure step |
|---|---|

grades.reader_quote: 1. Trade does not exhaust ships. At Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency’s Writers box, using dividers to preserve affiliation; filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply. Fitted player ships keep their fatigue.
grades.answer_key_quote: Trade capacity one order per ship, not Army-style exhaustion. Writers placed on routes return to associated Presidency, not arbitrary/home region writer box. Divider separates adjacent different-Presidency writers; tokens/dividers removed at Refresh.

source_quotes.quote:
| Piece | Refresh destination or state |
|---|---|
| Writers on orders | Return to their **associated Presidency's Writers box**; use dividers to preserve affiliation. |
| Filled tokens and Presidency dividers | Return to supply. |
| Extra ships | Return to supply. |
| Exhausted Army officers and regiments | Reactivate. |
| Active local alliances | Exhaust; do not reactivate alliances. |
| Fitted player ships | Keep fatigue; Trade itself never exhausts ships. |
| Turn marker | **Advance one turn, then begin London Season.** |

**Successful Trade capacity is one order per ship in this Presidency's sea zone. Trade does not exhaust ships.** Fill as many orders as possible within declared regions. First writer goes to home port. Every later order must extend the connected route filled during this same Presidency's Trade. **Writers from another Presidency cannot extend this route**, even when adjacent. **Writers do not limit capacity: use all available writers, then continue filling with filled-order tokens for the remaining ships.** Those tokens continue this Trade's own route. No President may fill another President's home region, even if its office vacant. Increase Balance by each order's printed value, **or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn under Deregulation**. President earns bank £1 per order; writer owners earn £1 per writer placed. Separate adjacent writers from different Presidencies with dividers for correct return at Refresh.

source_quotes.quote:
**Storms:** A sea-zone result checks that zone; three storms checks **all** sea zones; no storm indication means **no storm checks**. Determine eligibility before rolling:

| Ships | Storm exposure |
|---|---|
| Company and extra ships | **Exempt**; never roll storm checks. |
| Player-owned ships in Company fleets | Check ships in the affected sea zone(s). |
| Ships assigned to China | Count as **Eastern** sea zone. |
| Firm ships | Count in the sea zone on their **firm strategy**, even though on a charter. |
| Hobnob firm ships | **Exempt** from storms. |

Roll **once per eligible ship**: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. Return a sunk ship to its shipyard **unfatigued**.

After expenses, manager may pay dividends **from India treasury only**. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. **Waiving a dividend requires BOTH the shareholder's choice and the MANAGER'S CONSENT**; shareholder consent alone is insufficient. With that consent, the shareholder may forgo payment for any number of shares on any dividend. Record **total actual cash paid out**, not per-share dividend, with dividend cube on Company Balance track. An active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero; Hobnob retains prior marker. Sweep remaining India money into London. Firm ships face storms in strategy zone; Hobnob exempts them.

source_quotes.quote:
| Step | Procedure |
|---|---|
| 1. Firms, if deregulated | For **each player separately**, add VP from all their shares across all their firms, then **round that player's total DOWN once**. Deduct **1 VP per own family piece in Debtor's Prison**. |
| 2. Firm special retirement, if deregulated | Each eligible shareholder may retire **one member from supply**, after firm scoring but **BEFORE Power or any other ordinary final scoring**. Applies whether Company survived OR failed; no display cards. |
| 3. Power | Calculate Power and award its VP, as below. |
| 4. Court/workshops | Score Company shares and, on failure, uninvested workshops, as below. |
| 5. Final retirements OR failure card | Resolve the appropriate Company outcome below. Firm special retirement in step2 occurs in **either** outcome and is not replaced by the failure card. |
**Court/workshops:** If Company survived, add Court's current VP per Company share. If failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Scores may be negative.
Firm-track VP per share: Value 1 = −1 VP; 2 = 0; 3–4 = ½; 5–7 = 1; 8–9 = 1½; 10 = 2. The firm's Value number is also used for expenses; its VP rate is the symbol beneath that number.

grades.reader_quote: 1. Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reducing a check to zero dice means failure. Company Fraud is played at the start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and take bank cash equal to the actual Balance reduction, so payout cannot exceed cash actually removed from Balance. Public Demands Impeachment returns the member to supply and the office card to vacancies. grades.answer_key_quote: Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reducing a check to zero dice means failure. Company Fraud is played at the start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Company Balance by twice the highest roll but not below zero, and take only the amount actually removed from the bank. Thus Balance £10 and highest roll 6 gives Balance £0 and a £10 payout, not £12. Public Demands Impeachment returns the officeholder to supply and office card to Vacant Offices. Military Oversight demotes Commander to officer, making that former Commander eligible for reappointment.

source_quotes.quote:
**Company Fraud payout cap:** The player receives only the cash actually removed from Company Balance. For example, Balance £10 and highest roll 6 results in Balance £0 and a £10 payout, not £12. Cole Wehrle confirmed that exact alternative on September 24, 2022. [Designer ruling](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2938749/article/40850873#40850873). Use the corrected card timing: start of Revenue.

**Foreign Invasion and unrest:** Cole Wehrle clarified on April 30, 2023 that unrest does **not** add to a Foreign Invasion's primary attack strength or determine its resulting tower levels. Use the ordinary die roll for both attack strength and halving to create towers; the event still uses the Company-defense procedure and its secondary unrest attacks. Do not apply the normal primary Crisis's added unrest to this special event. [Designer ruling](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2962161/article/42192767#42192767). **On a successful Foreign Invasion, close all orders in the target region once; if they are already all closed, Cascade instead.** Region Loss does not close them a second time: its additional closure is only for a normal Invasion Crisis.

**Applicable official errata:** The publisher links the [official errata discussion](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2936700/official-errata), whose original designer post links the full internal correction list. The assigned Second Printing rulebook incorporates the core procedural corrections, including forced prize-piece reuse, empty Court, deployment boundaries, Region Loss and Elephant priority. Corrected setup cards supply Bengal's 1758 control token and 1813 control/share-value tokens. Printed card corrections also specify: Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reducing a check to zero dice means failure; Company Fraud is played at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and take cash from the bank equal to that actual Balance reduction; Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies; Military Oversight demotes one Commander to an officer, then appoints a Commander from officers: **the SAME former Commander remains eligible to become COMMANDER again**. These are card-specific effects, not changes to the normal check/hiring procedures.

source_quotes.quote: **India terminology:** A region's tower levels are its strength; the dome adds none. Orders are connected trading opportunities with printed revenue values; heavy outlines mark home ports. Closed orders cannot be filled. Sovereign regions have a dome without a flag or a capital/star flag; dominated regions have a small flag or no dome. An empire has one capital and at least one dominated region. **Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital's starred flag: it is no longer an empire. **Success checks (p17):** First commit resources/cash: **all cash for a Company-office check comes from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank**. grades.reader_quote: 1. First roll the storm die; its face specifies affected sea zones and the number of India events. Resolve all required storms before drawing any event. Company and extra ships are exempt from storm checks; check player-owned ships in Company fleets in affected sea zones; China ships count as Eastern; firm ships count in the sea zone on their firm strategy; Hobnob ships are exempt. Roll once per eligible ship: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink, returning sunk ships to their shipyards unfatigued. 2. Then flip and resolve one tile at a time from the draw stack, for as many events as the number printed on the storm die face. Where an event uses a region, normally read the back of the new top tile, not the tile just drawn, subject to its specific location rule.
grades.answer_key_quote: Roll the storm die first. If a sea zone is indicated, check the eligible ships there; three storms requires all sea zones, and no storm indication gives no storm checks. Company and extra ships are exempt. Resolve storms before India events. Then resolve as many events as the number printed on that die face, flipping one tile from the draw stack for each event. The location often comes from the back of the next top tile, with each event type’s stated location rules controlling. Apply the existing China/firm zone and Hobnob rules to determine eligible ships.

source_quotes.quote:
**First roll the storm die:** its face specifies affected sea zones and the **number of India events**. Resolve all required storms **before drawing any event**. Then flip and resolve **one tile at a time from the draw stack, for as many events as the number printed on that die face**. Where an event uses a region, normally read the **back of the new top tile** in the draw stack, not the tile just drawn; follow each event's specific location rule.

**Storms:** A sea-zone result checks that zone; three storms checks **all** sea zones; no storm indication means **no storm checks**. Determine eligibility before rolling:

Trade proceeds go to India; India pays dividends and may also pay expenses. Firm expenses may be paid from either or both treasuries; after dividends, remaining India money is swept to London. source_quotes.quote: Firm managers control firms; firm shares can be traded like Company shares. A firm has two treasuries: **London** receives the bank's £5 per investment and pays for ship acquisition, trade bids and expenses; **India** receives trade and pays dividends/expenses. **Investment cash always comes FROM the BANK TO London. London cash cannot buy new equity shares; creating shares requires a Company-share or workshop contribution.** **Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries.** Only specified investment, payout and expense procedures move it.

- **Ships:** A firm may fit a ship from **its own OR ANOTHER PLAYER'S shipyard**, but **must have that shipyard owner's consent**. Pay **£3 FROM the firm's London treasury TO the BANK**. May buy player-owned ship already in Company with owner's consent: unfatigued £3, fatigued £2, paid into Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships.

After expenses, manager may pay dividends **from India treasury only**. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. **Waiving a dividend requires BOTH the shareholder's choice and the MANAGER'S CONSENT**; shareholder consent alone is insufficient. With that consent, the shareholder may forgo payment for any number of shares on any dividend. Record **total actual cash paid out**, not per-share dividend, with dividend cube on Company Balance track. An active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero; Hobnob retains prior marker. Sweep remaining India money into London. Firm ships face storms in strategy zone; Hobnob exempts them.

Company/extras exempt China Eastern firm strategy Hobnob exempt

grades.reader_quote: Begin by rolling storm die; its face specifies affected sea zones and number of India events. Resolve all required storms before drawing events. Then flip and resolve tiles one at a time from draw stack, for as many events as that die face specifies. For an event using a region, normally read the back of the new top tile in the draw stack, not the tile just drawn, subject to the specific event location rule. source_quotes.quote:
**First roll the storm die:** its face specifies affected sea zones and the **number of India events**. Resolve all required storms **before drawing any event**. Then flip and resolve **one tile at a time from the draw stack, for as many events as the number printed on that die face**. Where an event uses a region, normally read the **back of the new top tile** in the draw stack, not the tile just drawn; follow each event's specific location rule.

**Storms:** A sea-zone result checks that zone; three storms checks **all** sea zones; no storm indication means **no storm checks**. Determine eligibility before rolling:

| Ships | Storm exposure |
|---|---|
| Company and extra ships | **Exempt**; never roll storm checks. |
| Player-owned ships in Company fleets | Check ships in the affected sea zone(s). |
| Ships assigned to China | Count as **Eastern** sea zone. |
| Firm ships | Count in the sea zone on their **firm strategy**, even though on a charter. |
| Hobnob firm ships | **Exempt** from storms. |

Roll **once per eligible ship**: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. Return a sunk ship to its shipyard **unfatigued**.
